description: Hand-labeled evaluation set for the Planner/Executor agent behind /api/v1/analyze. Each item names an expected outcome decided before running the agent. Grounded in real data restored from gdelt_mysql_backup.sql (2024 North America GDELT events). Revision 2 (after the date/comparison fixes): date-range lengths are counted inclusively (reldate-01 is a Mon-Sun week = 7 days; the earlier value 6 came from end-minus-start counting, which also made 'yesterday' 0 days against an expectation of 1). New items below were written from the intended behaviour before any re-run. Revision 3: reldate-04 gets real assertions (it was notes-only) and invalid-date-01 also asserts the queried range; both changes make the set stricter, no expectation was relaxed.

items.notes: Must hit the regex fast path before any Ollama call.
Regex fast path, greeting-adjacent word.
Punctuation-only input, must not crash the planner.
Real GlobalEventID confirmed to exist in the restored DB (Fort Worth explosion coverage, 2024-01-09).
Tests the EVT-YYYY-MM-DD-ID fingerprint format branch in query_event_detail specifically.
Nonexistent ID. Should return a clean not-found result, not a 500.
Generic hot-events phrasing, no date given.
Date-anchored hot events, should resolve to the exact date given.
No explicit date; server should default sensibly.
Date-anchored daily brief phrasing.

items.query: give me a regional overview of Texas this year
items.notes: Region + broad time range.

items.query: how has California been this month
items.notes: Region + relative time phrase, also stresses relative-date handling.

items.query: what were the top events in Texas in January 2024
items.notes: Confirmed live: routes rule-based, confidence=high, real 2024-01 Texas events returned (Fort Worth, Uvalde follow-up).

items.query: top events in Florida in March 2024
items.notes: Same structural shape as top-01, different region/month, for consistency check.

Maximally terse, fully structured query with no distinctive free-text component. Candidate for triggering the extract_context NameError-to-regex-fallback path (query_text likely null). Score by inspecting phases[0].detail and confidence, not by assuming which value it will be.
Same probe purpose as confidence-probe-01, different phrasing.
Same probe purpose, third phrasing for robustness.

items.query: find news articles about the Uvalde school shooting response
items.notes: Has a clear free-text component (specific named topic), query_text should NOT be null here.

items.query: which country had the most conflict events in North America in 2024
items.notes: Canonical example question used throughout the case document and course lessons.

expected.known_limitation: event_fingerprints headline/summary columns are empty because the population ETL has not been run; expect empty or near-empty results even if matching events exist in events_table

items.notes: Documents a known, disclosed gap rather than a bug: table exists (schema fixed) but is unpopulated.

Confirmed live to NOT return a 7-day window. Root cause: local Ollama router has no anchor/reference date passed into its prompt and the resulting range is not validated; regex fallback also has no 'last week' handling. This is the flagship bug-finding item in this set. Relative dates are anchored to the dataset end (2024-12-31), not the wall clock.
Simpler relative-date phrase, single-day window expected. Relative dates are anchored to the dataset end (2024-12-31), not the wall clock.

items.query: events in the past 3 days in New York
items.notes: Explicit numeric relative-date phrase, easier case than 'last week'. Relative dates are anchored to the dataset end (2024-12-31), not the wall clock.

items.query: how has Texas been this month
items.notes: Cross-check against overview-02; both use 'this month' phrasing, results should be internally consistent with each other. Revision 3: was a notes-only item (always skipped); now asserts the same tool as overview-02 and December 2024 as 'this month'.

items.query: Did protest activity increase in Canada this month?
items.notes: The question from the interview. Needs two complete counts and a computed change, not a top-50 sample.

items.query: Did protests increase in Canada in March compared with February?
items.notes: Earlier period first regardless of sentence order; February 2024 has 29 days.
Regression for the March 1-28 bug.
30-day month.
Leap year.

items.query: show me a protest march in Texas
items.notes: 'march' here is a noun, not the month; must not narrow the range to March.

Impossible date: must not be silently accepted; the user should be told what was used instead. Revision 3: also asserts the range, because a live run passed on the notice alone while querying 2024-12-30 and the notice claimed the full year.
